name: slider
params: {number} value Initial value
{number} min Minimum value - optional, defaults to 0
{number} max Maximum value - optional, defaults to 1
{number} step Step size - optional
description: Displays a slider widget to allow the user manipulate a value

name: s
params: {string | Pattern} sound The sound / pattern of sounds to pick
description:
Select a sound / sample by name. When using mininotation, you can also optionally supply 'n' and 'gain' parameters
separated by ':'.

name: wt
params: {number | Pattern} position Position in the wavetable from 0 to 1
description: Position in the wavetable of the wavetable oscillator

name: wtenv
params: {number | Pattern} amount between 0 and 1
description: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtattack
params: {number | Pattern} time attack time in seconds
description: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtdecay
params: {number | Pattern} time decay time in seconds
description: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtsustain
params: {number | Pattern} gain sustain level (0 to 1)
description: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtrelease
params: {number | Pattern} time release time in seconds
description: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: wtrate
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in hertz
description: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtsync
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in cycles
description: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtshape
params: {number | Pattern} shape Shape of the lfo (0, 1, 2, ..)
description: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtdc
params: {number | Pattern} dcoffset dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar
description: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: wtskew
params: {number | Pattern} skew How much to bend the LFO shape
description: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's position

name: warp
params: {number | Pattern} amount Warp of the wavetable from 0 to 1
description: Amount of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator

name: warpattack
params: {number | Pattern} time attack time in seconds
description: Attack time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpdecay
params: {number | Pattern} time decay time in seconds
description: Decay time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warpsustain
params: {number | Pattern} gain sustain level (0 to 1)
description: Sustain time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warprelease
params: {number | Pattern} time release time in seconds
description: Release time of the wavetable oscillator's warp envelope

name: warprate
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in hertz
description: Rate of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpshape
params: {number | Pattern} shape Shape of the lfo (0, 1, 2, ..)
description: Shape of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpdc
params: {number | Pattern} dcoffset dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar
description: DC offset of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpskew
params: {number | Pattern} skew How much to bend the LFO shape
description: Skew of the LFO for the wavetable oscillator's warp

name: warpmode
params: {number | string | Pattern} mode Warp mode
description:
Type of warp (alteration of the waveform) to apply to the wavetable oscillator.

The current options are: none, asym, bendp, bendm, bendmp, sync, quant, fold, pwm, orbit,
spin, chaos, primes, binary, brownian, reciprocal, wormhole, logistic, sigmoid, fractal, flip
examples:
s("morgana").bank("wt_digital").seg(8).note("F1").warp("0 0.25 0.5 0.75 1")
.warpmode("<asym bendp spin logistic sync wormhole brownian>*2")

name: wtphaserand
params: {number | Pattern} amount Randomness of the initial phase. Between 0 (not random) and 1 (fully random)
description: Amount of randomness of the initial phase of the wavetable oscillator.

name: warpenv
params: {number | Pattern} amount between 0 and 1
description: Amount of envelope applied wavetable oscillator's position envelope

name: warpsync
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in cycles
description: cycle synced rate of the LFO for the wavetable warp position

name: source
params: {function} getSource
description: Define a custom webaudio node to use as a sound source.

name: n
params: {number | Pattern} value sample index starting from 0
description:
Selects the given index:
- for samples, it picks the sample by index, with wrap around
- for scales, it picks the scale degree
- for voicings, it picks the voice index

name: i
params: {number | Pattern} value
description: Selects the given degree. Currently used in `xen` and `tune`:

name: note
description:
Plays the given note name or midi number. A note name consists of

- a letter (a-g or A-G)
- optional accidentals (b or #)
- optional (possibly negative) octave number (0-9). Defaults to 3

Examples of valid note names: `c`, `bb`, `Bb`, `f#`, `c3`, `A4`, `Eb2`, `c#5`

You can also use midi numbers instead of note names, where 69 is mapped to A4 440Hz in 12EDO.

name: accelerate
params: {number | Pattern} amount acceleration.
description: A pattern of numbers that speed up (or slow down) samples while they play. Currently only supported by osc / superdirt.

name: velocity
description: Sets the velocity from 0 to 1. Is multiplied together with gain.

name: gain
params: {number | Pattern} amount gain.
description: Controls the gain by an exponential amount.

name: postgain
description: Gain applied after all effects have been processed.

name: amp
params: {number | Pattern} amount gain.
description: Like `gain`, but linear.

name: fmh
params: {number | Pattern} harmonicity
description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation Harmonicity Ratio.
Controls the timbre of the sound.
Whole numbers and simple ratios sound more natural,
while decimal numbers and complex ratios sound metallic.

A number may be added afterwards to control the harmonicity of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmh2`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmh("<1 2 1.5 1.61>")
._scope()

name: fmi
params: {number | Pattern} brightness modulation index
description:
Sets the Frequency Modulation of the synth.
Controls the modulation index, which defines the brightness of the sound.

A number may be added afterwards to control the modulation index of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fm3`). Also, FMs may be routed into
each other with matrix commands like `fm13`, which would send `fm1` back into
`fm3`
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm("<0 1 2 8 32>")
._scope()

name: fmenv
params: {number | Pattern} type lin | exp
description:
Ramp type of fm envelope. Exp might be a bit broken..

A number may be added afterwards to control the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmenv4`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.2)
.fmsustain(0)
.fmenv("<exp lin>")
._scope()

name: fmattack
params: {number | Pattern} time attack time
description:
Attack time for the FM envelope: time it takes to reach maximum modulation

A number may be added afterwards to control the attack of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmatt5`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmattack("<0 .05 .1 .2>")
._scope()

name: fmwave
params: {number | Pattern} wave waveform
description:
Waveform of the fm modulator

A number may be added afterwards to control the waveform
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmwave6`)

name: fmdecay
params: {number | Pattern} time decay time
description:
Decay time for the FM envelope: seconds until the sustain level is reached after the attack phase.

A number may be added afterwards to control the decay of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmdec6`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay("<.01 .05 .1 .2>")
.fmsustain(.4)
._scope()

name: fmsustain
params: {number | Pattern} level sustain level
description:
Sustain level for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the decay phase

A number may be added afterwards to control the sustain of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmsus7`)
examples:
note("c e g b g e")
.fm(4)
.fmdecay(.1)
.fmsustain("<1 .75 .5 0>")
._scope()

name: fmrelease
params: {number | Pattern} time release time
description:
Release time for the FM envelope: how much modulation is applied after the note is released

A number may be added afterwards to control the release of the envelope of
any of the 8 individual FMs (e.g. `fmrel8`)

name: bank
params: {string | Pattern} bank the name of the bank
description: Select the sound bank to use. To be used together with `s`. The bank name (+ "_") will be prepended to the value of `s`.
examples: s("bd sd [~ bd] sd").bank('RolandTR909') // = s("RolandTR909_bd RolandTR909_sd")

name: chorus
params: {string | Pattern} chorus mix amount between 0 and 1
description: mix control for the chorus effect

name: attack
params: {number | Pattern} attack time in seconds.
description: Amplitude envelope attack time: Specifies how long it takes for the sound to reach its peak value, relative to the onset.

name: decay
params: {number | Pattern} time decay time in seconds
description:
Amplitude envelope decay time: the time it takes after the attack time to reach the sustain level.
Note that the decay is only audible if the sustain value is lower than 1.

name: sustain
params: {number | Pattern} gain sustain level between 0 and 1
description: Amplitude envelope sustain level: The level which is reached after attack / decay, being sustained until the offset.

name: release
params: {number | Pattern} time release time in seconds
description: Amplitude envelope release time: The time it takes after the offset to go from sustain level to zero.

name: bpf
params: {number | Pattern} frequency center frequency
description:
Sets the center frequency of the **b**and-**p**ass **f**ilter. When using mininotation, you
can also optionally supply the 'bpq' parameter separated by ':'.

name: bpq
params: {number | Pattern} q q factor
description: Sets the **b**and-**p**ass **q**-factor (resonance).

name: begin
params: {number | Pattern} amount between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample
description: A pattern of numbers from 0 to 1. Skips the beginning of each sample, e.g. `0.25` to cut off the first quarter from each sample.

name: end
params: {number | Pattern} length 1 = whole sample, .5 = half sample, .25 = quarter sample etc..
description: The same as .begin, but cuts off the end off each sample.

name: loop
params: {number | Pattern} on If 1, the sample is looped
description:
Loops the sample.
Note that the tempo of the loop is not synced with the cycle tempo.
To change the loop region, use loopBegin / loopEnd.

name: loopBegin
params: {number | Pattern} time between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample
description:
Begin to loop at a specific point in the sample (inbetween `begin` and `end`).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween `begin` and `end`, and before `loopEnd`!
Note: Samples starting with wt_ will automatically loop! (wt = wavetable)

name: loopEnd
params: {number | Pattern} time between 0 and 1, where 1 is the length of the sample
description:
End the looping section at a specific point in the sample (inbetween `begin` and `end`).
Note that the loop point must be inbetween `begin` and `end`, and after `loopBegin`!

name: crush
params: {number | Pattern} depth between 1 (for drastic reduction in bit-depth) to 16 (for barely no reduction).
description: Bit crusher effect.

name: coarse
params: {number | Pattern} factor 1 for original 2 for half, 3 for a third and so on.
description: Fake-resampling for lowering the sample rate. Caution: This effect seems to only work in chromium based browsers

name: tremolo
params: {number | Pattern} speed modulation speed in HZ
description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tremolosync
params: {number | Pattern} cycles modulation speed in cycles
description: Modulate the amplitude of a sound with a continuous waveform

name: tremolodepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth
description: Depth of amplitude modulation

name: tremoloskew
params: {number | Pattern} amount between 0 & 1, the shape of the waveform
description: Alter the shape of the modulation waveform

name: tremolophase
params: {number | Pattern} offset the offset in cycles of the modulation
description: Alter the phase of the modulation waveform

name: tremoloshape
params: {number | Pattern} shape tri | square | sine | saw | ramp
description: Shape of amplitude modulation
examples: note("{f g c d}%16").tremsync(4).tremoloshape("<sine tri square>").s("sawtooth")

name: drive
params: {number | Pattern} amount
description: Filter overdrive for supported filter types
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%16".sub(17)).s("supersaw").lpenv(8).lpf(150).lpq(.8).ftype('ladder').drive("<.5 4>")

name: duckorbit
params: {number | Pattern} orbit target orbit
description:
Modulate the amplitude of an orbit to create a "sidechain" like effect.

Can be applied to multiple orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`

name: duckdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation from 0 to 1
description:
The amount of ducking applied to target orbit

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckdepth("0.3:0.1")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

name: duckonset
params: {number | Pattern} time The onset time in seconds
description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to reach their lowest volume.
Can be used to prevent clicking or for creative rhythmic effects.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.
examples:
// Rhythmic
noise: s("pink").distort("2:1").orbit(4) // used rhythmically with 0.3 onset below
hhat: s("hh*16").orbit(7)
ducker: s("bd*4").bank("tr909").duckorbit("4:7").duckonset("0.3:0.003").duckattack(0.25)

name: duckattack
params: {number | Pattern} time The attack time in seconds
description:
The time required for the ducked signal(s) to return to their normal volume.

Can vary across orbits with the ':' mininotation, e.g. `duckonset("0:0.003")`.
Note: this requires first applying the effect to multiple orbits with e.g. `duckorbit("2:3")`.

name: byteBeatExpression
params: {number | Pattern} byteBeatExpression bitwise expression for creating bytebeat
description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: byteBeatStartTime
params: {number | Pattern} byteBeatStartTime in samples (t)
description: Create byte beats with custom expressions

name: channels
params: {number | Pattern} channels pattern the output channels
description: Allows you to set the output channels on the interface

name: pw
params: {number | Pattern} pulsewidth
description: Controls the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwrate
params: {number | Pattern} rate
description: Controls the lfo rate for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: pwsweep
params: {number | Pattern} sweep
description: Controls the lfo sweep for the pulsewidth of the pulse oscillator

name: phaser
params: {number | Pattern} speed speed of modulation
description: Phaser audio effect that approximates popular guitar pedals.

name: phasersweep
params: {number | Pattern} phasersweep most useful values are between 0 and 4000
description: The frequency sweep range of the lfo for the phaser effect. Defaults to 2000

name: phasercenter
params: {number | Pattern} centerfrequency in HZ
description: The center frequency of the phaser in HZ. Defaults to 1000

name: phaserdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth number between 0 and 1
description: The amount the signal is affected by the phaser effect. Defaults to 0.75

name: channel
params: {number | Pattern} channel channel number
description: Choose the channel the pattern is sent to

name: cut
params: {number | Pattern} group cut group number
description: In the style of classic drum-machines, `cut` will stop a playing sample as soon as another samples with in same cutgroup is to be played. An example would be an open hi-hat followed by a closed one, essentially muting the open.

name: lpf
params: {number | Pattern} frequency audible between 0 and 20000
description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the **l**ow-**p**ass **f**ilter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'lpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: lpenv
params: {number | Pattern} modulation depth of the lowpass filter envelope between 0 and _n_
description: Sets the lowpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: hpenv
params: {number | Pattern} modulation depth of the highpass filter envelope between 0 and _n_
description: Sets the highpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: bpenv
params: {number | Pattern} modulation depth of the bandpass filter envelope between 0 and _n_
description: Sets the bandpass filter envelope modulation depth.

name: lpattack
params: {number | Pattern} attack time of the filter envelope
description: Sets the attack duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: hpattack
params: {number | Pattern} attack time of the highpass filter envelope
description: Sets the attack duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: bpattack
params: {number | Pattern} attack time of the bandpass filter envelope
description: Sets the attack duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: lpdecay
params: {number | Pattern} decay time of the filter envelope
description: Sets the decay duration for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: hpdecay
params: {number | Pattern} decay time of the highpass filter envelope
description: Sets the decay duration for the highpass filter envelope.

name: bpdecay
params: {number | Pattern} decay time of the bandpass filter envelope
description: Sets the decay duration for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: lpsustain
params: {number | Pattern} sustain amplitude of the lowpass filter envelope
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: hpsustain
params: {number | Pattern} sustain amplitude of the highpass filter envelope
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the highpass filter envelope.

name: bpsustain
params: {number | Pattern} sustain amplitude of the bandpass filter envelope
description: Sets the sustain amplitude for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: lprelease
params: {number | Pattern} release time of the filter envelope
description: Sets the release time for the lowpass filter envelope.

name: hprelease
params: {number | Pattern} release time of the highpass filter envelope
description: Sets the release time for the highpass filter envelope.

name: bprelease
params: {number | Pattern} release time of the bandpass filter envelope
description: Sets the release time for the bandpass filter envelope.

name: ftype
params: {number | Pattern} type 12db (0), ladder (1), or 24db (2)
description: Sets the filter type. The ladder filter is more aggressive. More types might be added in the future.
examples: note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpenv(4).lpf(500).ftype("<0 1 2>").lpq(1)

note("c f g g a c d4").fast(2)
.sound('sawtooth')
.lpf(200).fanchor(0)
.lpenv(3).lpq(1)
.ftype("<ladder 12db 24db>")

name: fanchor
params: {number | Pattern} center 0 to 1
description: controls the center of the filter envelope. 0 is unipolar positive, .5 is bipolar, 1 is unipolar negative
examples:
note("{f g g c d a a#}%8").s("sawtooth").lpf("{1000}%2")
.lpenv(8).fanchor("<0 .5 1>")

name: hpf
params: {number | Pattern} frequency audible between 0 and 20000
description:
Applies the cutoff frequency of the **h**igh-**p**ass **f**ilter.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'hpq' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: lprate
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in hertz
description: Rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpsync
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in cycles
description: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpdepthfrequency
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation

name: lpshape

description: Shape of the LFO for the lowpass filter

params: {number | Pattern} dcoffset dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar
description: DC offset of the LFO for the lowpass filter

name: lpskew
params: {number | Pattern} skew How much to bend the LFO shape
description: Skew of the LFO for the lowpass filter

description: Rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpsync
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in cycles
description: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdepthfrequency
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the bandpass filter, in HZ

name: bpshape
params: {number | Pattern} shape Shape of the lfo (0, 1, 2, ..)
description: Shape of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpdc
params: {number | Pattern} dcoffset dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar
description: DC offset of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: bpskew
params: {number | Pattern} skew How much to bend the LFO shape
description: Skew of the LFO for the bandpass filter

name: hprate
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in hertz
description: Rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpsync
params: {number | Pattern} rate rate in cycles
description: Cycle-synced rate of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdepth
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdepthfrequency
params: {number | Pattern} depth depth of modulation
description: Depth of the LFO for the hipass filter, in hz

name: hpshape
params: {number | Pattern} shape Shape of the lfo (0, 1, 2, ..)
description: Shape of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpdc
params: {number | Pattern} dcoffset dc offset. set to 0 for unipolar
description: DC offset of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: hpskew
params: {number | Pattern} skew How much to bend the LFO shape
description: Skew of the LFO for the highpass filter

name: vib
params: {number | Pattern} frequency of the vibrato in hertz
description: Applies a vibrato to the frequency of the oscillator.
examples:
// change the modulation depth with ":"
note("a e")
.vib("<.5 1 2 4 8 16>:12")
._scope()

name: noise
params: {number | Pattern} wet wet amount
description: Adds pink noise to the mix

name: vibmod
params: {number | Pattern} depth of vibrato (in semitones)
description: Sets the vibrato depth in semitones. Only has an effect if `vibrato` | `vib` | `v` is is also set
examples:
// change the vibrato frequency with ":"
note("a e")
.vibmod("<.25 .5 1 2 12>:8")
._scope()

name: hpq
params: {number | Pattern} q resonance factor between 0 and 50
description: Controls the **h**igh-**p**ass **q**-value.

name: lpq
params: {number | Pattern} q resonance factor between 0 and 50
description: Controls the **l**ow-**p**ass **q**-value.

name: djf
params: {number | Pattern} cutoff below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter
description: DJ filter, below 0.5 is low pass filter, above is high pass filter.

name: delay
params: {number | Pattern} level between 0 and 1
description:
Sets the level of the delay signal.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'delaytime' and 'delayfeedback' parameter,
separated by ':'.

name: delayfeedback
params: {number | Pattern} feedback between 0 and 1
description:
Sets the level of the signal that is fed back into the delay.
Caution: Values >= 1 will result in a signal that gets louder and louder! Don't do it

name: delayspeed
params: {number | Pattern} delayspeed controls the pitch of the delay feedback
description: Sets the time of the delay effect.

name: delaytime
params: {number | Pattern} delay in seconds
description: Sets the time of the delay effect in seconds.

name: delaysync
params: {number | Pattern} cycles delay length in cycles
description: Sets the time of the delay effect in cycles.

name: lock
params: {number | Pattern} enable When set to 1, delaytime is a direct multiple of a cycle.
description: Specifies whether delaytime is calculated relative to cps.

name: detune
params: {number | Pattern} amount
description: Set detune for stacked voices of supported oscillators.
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").detune("<.1 .2 .5 24.1>")

name: unison
params: {number | Pattern} numvoices
description: Set number of stacked voices for supported oscillators.
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").unison("<1 2 7>")

name: spread
params: {number | Pattern} spread between 0 and 1
description: Set the stereo pan spread for supported oscillators
examples: note("d f a a# a d3").fast(2).s("supersaw").spread("<0 .3 1>")

name: dry
params: {number | Pattern} dry 0 = wet, 1 = dry
description: Set dryness of reverb. See `room` and `size` for more information about reverb.

name: fadeTime
params: {number | Pattern} time between 0 and 1
description: Used when using `begin`/`end` or `chop`/`striate` and friends, to change the fade out time of the 'grain' envelope.

name: freq
params: {number | Pattern} frequency in Hz. the audible range is between 20 and 20000 Hz
description: Set frequency of sound.

name: pattack
params: {number | Pattern} time time in seconds
description: Attack time of pitch envelope.

name: pdecay
params: {number | Pattern} time time in seconds
description: Decay time of pitch envelope.

name: prelease
params: {number | Pattern} time time in seconds
description: Release time of pitch envelope
examples:
note("<c eb g bb> ~")
.release(.5) // to hear the pitch release
.prelease("<0 .1 .25 .5>")

name: penv
params: {number | Pattern} semitones change in semitones
description:
Amount of pitch envelope. Negative values will flip the envelope.
If you don't set other pitch envelope controls, `pattack:.2` will be the default.

name: pcurve
params: {number | Pattern} type 0 = linear, 1 = exponential
description: Curve of envelope. Defaults to linear. exponential is good for kicks

name: panchor
params: {number | Pattern} anchor anchor offset
description:
Sets the range anchor of the envelope:
- anchor 0: range = [note, note + penv]
- anchor 1: range = [note - penv, note]
If you don't set an anchor, the value will default to the psustain value.

name: leslie
params: {number | Pattern} wet between 0 and 1
description: Emulation of a Leslie speaker: speakers rotating in a wooden amplified cabinet.

name: lrate
params: {number | Pattern} rate 6.7 for fast, 0.7 for slow
description: Rate of modulation / rotation for leslie effect

name: lsize
params: {number | Pattern} meters somewhere between 0 and 1
description: Physical size of the cabinet in meters. Be careful, it might be slightly larger than your computer. Affects the Doppler amount (pitch warble)

name: label
params: {string} label text to display
description: Sets the displayed text for an event on the pianoroll

name: octave
params: {number | Pattern} octave octave number
description: Sets the default octave of a synth.

name: orbit
params: {number | Pattern} number
description: An `orbit` is a global parameter context for patterns. Patterns with the same orbit will share the same global effects.

name: bus
params: {number | Pattern} number
description:
A `bus` is a send which can be used for mixing patterns. It combines with..
s("bus") to play that bus through another pattern (for, say, applying non-linear
effects like distortion to multiple signals)

otherPat.bmod(..) (to modulate another pattern with the bus)

name: busgain
params: {number | Pattern} number
description: Postgain multiplier prior to sending the signal to the audio bus.

name: pan
params: {number | Pattern} pan between 0 and 1, from left to right (assuming stereo), once round a circle (assuming multichannel)
description: Sets position in stereo.
examples: s("bd rim sd rim bd ~ cp rim").pan(sine.slow(2))

name: panspan
params: {number | Pattern} span between -inf and inf, negative is backwards ordering
description: Controls how much multichannel output is fanned out

name: pansplay
params: {number | Pattern} spread between 0 and 1
description: Controls how much multichannel output is spread

name: chord
params: {string | Pattern} symbols chord symbols to voice e.g., C, Eb, Fm7, G7. The symbols can be defined via addVoicings
description: The chord to voice
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").voicing()

name: dictionary
params: {string} dictionaryName which dictionary (having been defined with `addVoicings`) to use
description: Which dictionary to use for the voicings. This falls back to the default dictionary if not provided
examples:
addVoicings('house', {
'': ['7 12 16', '0 7 16', '4 7 12'],
'm': ['0 3 7']
})
chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>")
.dict('house').anchor(66)
.voicing().room(.5)

name: anchor
params: {string | Pattern} anchorNote the note to align the voicing or scale to
description: The top note to align the voicing to. Defaults to c5

name: offset
params: {number | Pattern} shift the amount to shift the voicing up or down
description: Sets how the voicing is offset from the anchored position
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").offset("<0 1 2 3 4 5>") // alter the voicing each time

name: octaves
params: {number | Pattern} count the number of octaves
description: How many octaves are voicing steps spread apart, defaults to 1
examples: chord("<Am C D F Am E Am E>").octaves("<2 4>").voicing()

name: mode
params: {string | Pattern} modeName one of {below | above | duck | root | oldabove | oldroot}
description:
How the voicing is aligned to the anchor
- `below`: top note <= anchor
- `duck`: top note <= anchor, anchor excluded
- `above`: bottom note >= anchor
- `root`: bottom note is the lowest root of the chord >= anchor

- `oldabove` : old (buggy) behavior of above, kept for legacy reason
- `oldroot` : old (buggy) behavior of root, kept for legacy reason

name: room
params: {number | Pattern} level between 0 and 1
description:
Sets the level of reverb.

When using mininotation, you can also optionally add the 'size' parameter, separated by ':'.

name: roomlp
params: {number} frequency between 0 and 20000hz
description:
Reverb lowpass starting frequency (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomdim
params: {number} frequency between 0 and 20000hz
description:
Reverb lowpass frequency at -60dB (in hertz).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: roomfade
params: {number} seconds for the reverb to fade
description:
Reverb fade time (in seconds).
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: iresponse
params: {string | Pattern} sample to use as an impulse response
description: Sets the sample to use as an impulse response for the reverb.

name: irspeed
params: {string | Pattern} speed
description: Sets speed of the sample for the impulse response.

name: irbegin
params: {string | Pattern} begin between 0 and 1
description: Sets the beginning of the IR response sample

name: roomsize
params: {number | Pattern} size between 0 and 10
description:
Sets the room size of the reverb, see `room`.
When this property is changed, the reverb will be recaculated, so only change this sparsely..

name: shape
params: {number | Pattern} distortion between 0 and 1
description:
(Deprecated) Wave shaping distortion. WARNING: can suddenly get unpredictably loud.
Please use distort instead, which has a more predictable response curve
second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output

name: distort
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
{number | string | Pattern} type type of distortion to apply
description:
Wave shaping distortion. CAUTION: it can get loud.
Second option in optional array syntax (ex: ".9:.5") applies a postgain to the output. Third option sets the waveshaping type.
Most useful values are usually between 0 and 10 (depending on source gain). If you are feeling adventurous, you can turn it up to 11 and beyond ;)

name: distortvol
params: {number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Postgain for waveshaping distortion.

name: distorttype
params: {number | string | Pattern} type type of distortion to apply
description: Type of waveshaping distortion to apply.
examples:
s("sine").note("F1*2").release(1)
.penv(24).pdecay(0.05)
.distort(rand.range(1, 8))
.distorttype("<fold chebyshev scurve diode asym sinefold>")

name: compressor
description:
Dynamics Compressor. The params are `compressor("threshold:ratio:knee:attack:release")`
More info [here](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/DynamicsCompressorNode?retiredLocale=de#instance_properties)

name: speed
params: {number | Pattern} speed -inf to inf, negative numbers play the sample backwards.
description: Changes the speed of sample playback, i.e. a cheap way of changing pitch.

name: stretch
params: {number | Pattern} factor between `-4` and `inf`. Positive increases pitch, 0 does nothing, negative decreases the pitch.
description:
Changes the pitch of the sample without changing its speed.
The frequencies are multiplied by (factor + 1) for positive numbers
and by max(factor / 4 + 1, 0) for negative numbers.
So tuning up by octaves can be done with 1, 3, 7, ...
and tuning down by octaves with -2, -3, -3.5...

name: unit
params: {number | string | Pattern} unit see description above
description: Used in conjunction with `speed`, accepts values of "r" (rate, default behavior), "c" (cycles), or "s" (seconds). Using `unit "c"` means `speed` will be interpreted in units of cycles, e.g. `speed "1"` means samples will be stretched to fill a cycle. Using `unit "s"` means the playback speed will be adjusted so that the duration is the number of seconds specified by `speed`.

name: squiz
params: {number | Pattern} squiz Try passing multiples of 2 to it - 2, 4, 8 etc.
description:
Made by Calum Gunn. Reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter. The SuperCollider manual defines Squiz as:

"A simplistic pitch-raising algorithm. It's not meant to sound natural; its sound is reminiscent of some weird mixture of filter, ring-modulator and pitch-shifter, depending on the input. The algorithm works by cutting the signal into fragments (delimited by upwards-going zero-crossings) and squeezing those fragments in the time domain (i.e. simply playing them back faster than they came in), leaving silences inbetween. All the parameters apart from memlen can be modulated."

name: vowel
params: {string | Pattern} vowel You can use a e i o u ae aa oe ue y uh un en an on, corresponding to [a] [e] [i] [o] [u] [æ] [ɑ] [ø] [y] [ɯ] [ʌ] [œ̃] [ɛ̃] [ɑ̃] [ɔ̃]. Aliases: aa = å = ɑ, oe = ø = ö, y = ı, ae = æ.
description: Formant filter to make things sound like vowels.
examples: s("bd sd mt ht bd [~ cp] ht lt").vowel("[a|e|i|o|u]")

name: density
params: {number | Pattern} density between 0 and x
description: crackle noise density

name: clip
params: {number | Pattern} factor >= 0
description: Multiplies the duration with the given number. Also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: duration
params: {number | Pattern} seconds >= 0
description: Sets the duration of the event in cycles. Similar to clip / legato, it also cuts samples off at the end if they exceed the duration.

name: color
params: {string} color Hexadecimal or CSS color name
description: Sets the color of the hap in visualizations like pianoroll or highlighting.

name: adsr
params: {number | Pattern} time attack time in seconds
{number | Pattern} time decay time in seconds

name: nrpnn

name: nrpv

description: The host to send open sound control messages to. Requires running the OSC bridge.

params: {String | Array} mapping the control names that are set
description: Sets properties in a batch.

name: scrub
description:
Allows you to scrub an audio file like a tape loop by passing values that represents the position in the audio file
in the optional array syntax ex: "0.5:2", the second value controls the speed of playback

name: lfo
params: {Object} config LFO configuration.
{string | Pattern} [config.control] Node to modulate. Aliases: c
{string | Pattern} [config.subControl] Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
{number | Pattern} [config.rate] Modulation rate. Aliases: r
{number | Pattern} [config.sync] Tempo-synced modulation rate. Aliases: s
{number | Pattern} [config.depth] Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
{number | Pattern} [config.depthabs] Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
{number | Pattern} [config.dcoffset] DC offset / bias for the waveform. Aliases: dc
{number | Pattern} [config.shape] Shape index. Aliases: sh
{number | Pattern} [config.skew] Skew amount. Aliases: sk
{number | Pattern} [config.curve] Exponential curve amount. Aliases: cu
{number | Pattern} [config.retrig] If > 0.5, the LFO will retrigger on each event. Aliases: rt
{number | Pattern} [config.fxi] FX index to target
{string | Pattern} id ID to use for this modulator
description:
Configures an LFO. Can be called in sequence like pat.lfo(...).lfo(...) to set up multiple LFOs.
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:
1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `lfo({ c: "lpf" })`)
2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `lfo` call will be used
(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).lfo()` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

name: env
params: {Object} config Envelope configuration.
{string | Pattern} [config.control] Node to modulate. Aliases: c
{string | Pattern} [config.subControl] Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
{number | Pattern} [config.depth] Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
{number | Pattern} [config.depthabs] Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
{number | Pattern} [config.attack] Time to reach depth. Aliases: att, a
{number | Pattern} [config.decay] Time to reach sustain. Aliases: dec, d
{number | Pattern} [config.sustain] Sustain depth. Aliases: sus, s
{number | Pattern} [config.release] Time to return to nominal value. Aliases: rel, r
{number | Pattern} [config.acurve] Snappiness of attack curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: ac
{number | Pattern} [config.dcurve] Snappiness of decay curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: dc
{number | Pattern} [config.rcurve] Snappiness of release curve (-1 = relaxed, 1 = snappy). Aliases: rc
{number | Pattern} [config.fxi] FX index to target
{string | Pattern} id ID to use for this modulator
description:
Configures an envelope. Can be called in sequence like pat.env(...).env(...) to set up multiple envelopes
There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:
1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `env({ c: "lpf" })`)
2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `env` call will be used
(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.
examples:
s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 })
.env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
.diode(0.3)
.sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 1)) // envelope #1 (0-indexed)

s("pulse").lpf(500).env({ a: 1 }, 'lpf_mod')
.env({ c: "s", a: 1 })
.diode(0.3)
.sometimes(x => x.env({ a: "0.5" }, 'lpf_mod'))

name: bmod
params: {Object} config Bus modulation configuration.
{string | Pattern} [config.bus] Bus to get modulation signal from
{string | Pattern} [config.control] Node to modulate. Aliases: c
{string | Pattern} [config.subControl] Sub-control name to append to the control key. Aliases: sc
{number | Pattern} [config.depth] Relative modulation depth. Aliases: dep, dr
{number | Pattern} [config.depthabs] Absolute modulation depth. Aliases: da
{number | Pattern} [config.dc] DC offset prior to application
{number | Pattern} [config.fxi] FX index to target
{string | Pattern} id ID to use for this modulator
description:
Modulates with the output from a given `bus`.
Can be called in sequence like pat.bmod(...).bmod(...) to set up multiple modulators

Send to an audio bus with `otherPat.bus(..)`.

There are two ways to declare which control will be modulated:
1. Explicitly put `control` in the config (e.g. `bmod({ id: 2, c: "lpf" })`)
2. If the control parameter is absent, the control _immediately before_ the `bmod` call will be used
(e.g. `s("saw").lpf(500).bmod({ id: 2 })` to modulate `lpf`)

Modulators can be referred to by `id` so that they can be updated later e.g. inside
a `sometimes`. See example below.

name: transient
params: {number | Pattern} attack Emphasis on transients; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)
{number | Pattern} sustain Emphasis on the sustains; between -1 (deaccentuate) and 1 (accentuate)
description:
Transient shaper. Gives independent control over the emphasis on transients
and sustains

name: euclid
params: {number} pulses the number of onsets/beats
{number} steps the number of steps to fill
description:
Changes the structure of the pattern to form an Euclidean rhythm.
Euclidean rhythms are rhythms obtained using the greatest common
divisor of two numbers.  They were described in 2004 by Godfried
Toussaint, a Canadian computer scientist.  Euclidean rhythms are
really useful for computer/algorithmic music because they can
describe a large number of rhythms with a couple of numbers.

name: euclidRot
params: {number} pulses the number of onsets/beats
{number} steps the number of steps to fill
{number} rotation offset in steps
description: Like `euclid`, but has an additional parameter for 'rotating' the resulting sequence.
examples:
// A Samba rhythm necklace from Brazil
note("c3").euclidRot(3,16,14)

name: euclidLegato
params: {number} pulses the number of onsets/beats
{number} steps the number of steps to fill
rotation offset in steps
pat
description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps.

name: euclidLegatoRot
params: {number} pulses the number of onsets/beats
{number} steps the number of steps to fill
{number} rotation offset in steps
description:
Similar to `euclid`, but each pulse is held until the next pulse,
so there will be no gaps, and has an additional parameter for 'rotating'
the resulting sequence

name: euclidish
params: {number} pulses the number of onsets
{number} steps the number of steps to fill
{number} groove exists between the extremes of 0 (straight euclidian) and 1 (straight pulse)
description:
A 'euclid' variant with an additional parameter that morphs the resulting
rhythm from 0 (no morphing) to 1 (completely 'even'). For example
`sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0)` would be the same as
`sound("bd").euclid(3,8)`, and `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,1)` would be the
same as `sound("bd bd bd")`. `sound("bd").euclidish(3,8,0.5)` would have a
groove somewhere between.
Inspired by the work of Malcom Braff.

name: clearScope
description:
Clears all user-defined variables and functions from the scope.
This removes variables created during block-based evaluation.

name: layer
description: Layers the result of the given function(s). Like `superimpose`, but without the original pattern:

name: superimpose
description: Superimposes the result of the given function(s) on top of the original pattern:

name: log
description: Writes the content of the current event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: logValues
description:
A simplified version of `log` which writes all "values" (various configurable parameters)
within the event to the console (visible in the side menu).

name: into
description:
Breaks a pattern into pieces according to the structure of a given pattern.
True values in the given pattern cause the corresponding subcycle of the
source pattern to be looped, and for an (optional) given function to be
applied. False values result in the corresponding part of the source pattern
to be played unchanged.

name: set
params: {Pattern} pat
description:
When called on a pattern `a`, with a input pattern `b` (`a.set(b)`),
combines `a` and `b` such that anything defined in `b`
and anything defined in `a` that is *not* defined in `b`
will be in the resulting pattern.

The structure is maintained from `a`,
because the default pattern alignment is `in`,
see the section on `Pattern Alignment`
in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of `keep`

See examples below

name: keep
params: {Pattern} pat
description:
When called on a pattern `a`, with a input pattern `b` (`a.keep(b)`),
combines `a` and `b` such that anything defined in `a`,
and anything defined in `b` that is *not* defined in `a`
will be in the resulting pattern

The structure is maintained from `a`,
because the default pattern alignment is `in`,
see the section on `Pattern Alignment`
in the technical manual in the docs

This is the inverse of `set`

See examples below

name: add
description: Assumes a pattern of numbers. Adds the given number to each item in the pattern.

name: sub
description: Like add, but the given numbers are subtracted.
examples:
n("0 2 4".sub("<0 1 2 3>")).scale("C4:minor")
// See add for more information.

name: mul
description: Multiplies each number by the given factor.

name: div
description: Divides each number by the given factor.

name: gap
params: {number} steps
description: Does absolutely nothing, but with a given metrical 'steps'

name: silence
description: Does absolutely nothing..

name: sequence
description: See `fastcat`

name: round
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values rounded
to the nearest integer.

name: floor
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical floor. E.g. `3.7` replaced with to `3`, and `-4.2`
replaced with `-5`.

name: ceil
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern. Returns a new pattern with all values set to
their mathematical ceiling. E.g. `3.2` replaced with `4`, and `-4.2`
replaced with `-4`.

name: range
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1.
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.
Most useful in combination with continuous patterns.

name: rangex
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing unipolar values in the range 0 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range,
following an exponential curve.

name: range2
description:
Assumes a numerical pattern, containing bipolar values in the range -1 .. 1
Returns a new pattern with values scaled to the given min/max range.

name: ratio
description:
Allows dividing numbers via list notation using ":".
Returns a new pattern with just numbers.

name: fastGap
description: speeds up a pattern like fast, but rather than it playing multiple times as fast would it instead leaves a gap in the remaining space of the cycle. For example, the following will play the sound pattern "bd sn" only once but compressed into the first half of the cycle, i.e. twice as fast.

name: fast
params: {number | Pattern} factor speed up factor
description: Speed up a pattern by the given factor. Used by "*" in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").fast(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]*2")

name: slow
params: {number | Pattern} factor slow down factor
description: Slow down a pattern over the given number of cycles. Like the "/" operator in mini notation.
examples: s("bd hh sd hh").slow(2) // s("[bd hh sd hh]/2")

name: lastOf
params: {number} n how many cycles
{function} func function to apply
description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the last cycle.

name: firstOf
params: {number} n how many cycles
{function} func function to apply
description: Applies the given function every n cycles, starting from the first cycle.

name: every
params: {number} n how many cycles
{function} func function to apply
description: An alias for `firstOf`

name: apply
description: Applies the given function to the pattern. Like layer, but with a single function:

name: early
params: {number | Pattern} cycles number of cycles to nudge left
description: Nudge a pattern to start earlier in time. Equivalent of Tidal's <~ operator

name: late
params: {number | Pattern} cycles number of cycles to nudge right
description: Nudge a pattern to start later in time. Equivalent of Tidal's ~> operator

name: segment
params: {number} segments number of segments per cycle
description: Samples the pattern at a rate of n events per cycle. Useful for turning a continuous pattern into a discrete one.

name: invert
description: Swaps 1s and 0s in a binary pattern.

name: when
params: {Pattern} binary_pat
{function} func
description: Applies the given function whenever the given pattern is in a true state.

name: off
params: {Pattern | number} time offset time
{function} func function to apply
description: Superimposes the function result on top of the original pattern, delayed by the given time.

name: rev
description: Reverse all cycles in a pattern. See also `revv` for reversing a whole pattern.

name: revv
description: Reverse a whole pattern. See also `rev` for reversing each cycle.

name: juxBy
description: Jux with adjustable stereo width. 0 = mono, 1 = full stereo.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxBy("<0 .5 1>/2", rev)

name: juxFlipBy
description: Like juxBy, except it flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlipBy(".8", rev)

name: juxFlip
description: Like jux, but flips the ears each cycle.
examples: s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(rev)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(press)
s("bd lt [~ ht] mt cp ~ bd hh").juxFlip(iter(4))

name: echoWith
params: {number} times how many times to repeat
{number} time cycle offset between iterations
{function} func function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index
description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, applying the given function each time.

name: echo
params: {number} times how many times to repeat
{number} time cycle offset between iterations
{number} feedback velocity multiplicator for each iteration
description: Superimpose and offset multiple times, gradually decreasing the velocity

name: stut
params: {number} times how many times to repeat
{number} feedback velocity multiplicator for each iteration
{number} time cycle offset between iterations
description: Deprecated. Like echo, but the last 2 parameters are flipped.

name: plyWith
params: {number} factor how many times to repeat
{function} func function to apply, given the pattern
description: The plyWith function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.\n

name: plyForEach
params: {number} factor how many times to repeat
{function} func function to apply, given the pattern and the iteration index
description:
The plyForEach function repeats each event the given number of times, applying the given function to each event.
This version of ply uses the iteration index as an argument to the function, similar to echoWith.

name: iter
description: Divides a pattern into a given number of subdivisions, plays the subdivisions in order, but increments the starting subdivision each cycle. The pattern wraps to the first subdivision after the last subdivision is played.

name: iterBack
description: Like `iter`, but plays the subdivisions in reverse order. Known as iter' in tidalcycles

name: repeatCycles
description: Repeats each cycle the given number of times.

name: chunk
description: Divides a pattern into a given number of parts, then cycles through those parts in turn, applying the given function to each part in turn (one part per cycle).

name: chunkBack
description: Like `chunk`, but cycles through the parts in reverse order. Known as chunk' in tidalcycles

name: fastChunk
description:
Like `chunk`, but the cycles of the source pattern aren't repeated
for each set of chunks.

name: chunkInto
description: Like `chunk`, but the function is applied to a looped subcycle of the source pattern.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
.bank("tr909")

name: chunkBackInto
description: Like `chunkInto`, but moves backwards through the chunks.
examples:
sound("bd sd ht lt bd - cp lt").chunkInto(4, hurry(2))
.bank("tr909")

name: ribbon
params: {number} offset start point of loop in cycles
{number} cycles loop length in cycles
description:
Loops the pattern inside an `offset` for `cycles`.
If you think of the entire span of time in cycles as a ribbon, you can cut a single piece and loop it.

name: tag
params: {string} tag anything unique
description: Tags each Hap with an identifier. Good for filtering. The function populates Hap.context.tags (Array).
examples:
s("saw!16").note("F1")
.lpf(tri.range(40, 80).slow(4)).lpenv(5).lpq(4).lpd(0.15)
.when(rand.late(0.1).gte(0.5), x => x.transpose("12").tag('altered'))
.when(rand.late(0.2).gte(0.5), x => x.s("square").tag('altered'))
.when("<0 1>", x => x.filter((hap) => hap.hasTag('altered')))

name: filter
params: {Function} test function to test Hap
description: Filters haps using the given function

name: filterWhen
params: {Function} test function to test Hap.whole.begin
description: Filters haps by their begin time

name: within
params: {number} start start within cycle (0 - 1)
{number} end end within cycle (0 - 1). Must be > start
{Function} func function to be applied to the sub-pattern
description: Use within to apply a function to only a part of a pattern.

name: stepcat
description:
'Concatenates' patterns like `fastcat`, but proportional to a number of steps per cycle.
The steps can either be inferred from the pattern, or provided as a [length, pattern] pair.
Has the alias `timecat`.
examples:
stepcat("bd sd cp","hh hh").sound()
// the same as "bd sd cp hh hh".sound()

name: chop
description:
Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, allowing you to explore a technique known as 'granular synthesis'.
It turns a pattern of samples into a pattern of parts of samples.
examples:
samples({ rhodes: 'https://cdn.freesound.org/previews/132/132051_316502-lq.mp3' })
s("rhodes")
.chop(4)
.rev() // reverse order of chops
.loopAt(2) // fit sample into 2 cycles

name: striate
description: Cuts each sample into the given number of parts, triggering progressive portions of each sample at each loop.

name: loopAt
description: Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles by changing the speed.

name: slice
description:
Chops samples into the given number of slices, triggering those slices with a given pattern of slice numbers.
Instead of a number, it also accepts a list of numbers from 0 to 1 to slice at specific points.

name: onTriggerTime
description:
make something happen on event time
uses browser timeout which is innacurate for audio tasks

name: splice
description: Works the same as slice, but changes the playback speed of each slice to match the duration of its step.

name: fit
description:
Makes the sample fit its event duration. Good for rhythmical loops like drum breaks.
Similar to `loopAt`.

name: loopAtCps
description:
Makes the sample fit the given number of cycles and cps value, by
changing the speed. deprecated: use loopAt or fit instead, together with setCps / setCpm.

name: xfade
description:
Cross-fades between left and right from 0 to 1:
- 0 = (full left, no right)
- .5 = (both equal)
- 1 = (no left, full right)

name: beat
description:
creates a structure pattern from divisions of a cycle
especially useful for creating rhythms

name: soft
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Soft-clipping distortion

name: hard
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Hard-clipping distortion

name: cubic
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Cubic polynomial distortion

name: diode
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Diode-emulating distortion

name: asym
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Asymmetrical diode distortion

name: fold
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Wavefolding distortion

name: sinefold
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Wavefolding distortion composed with sinusoid

name: chebyshev
params: {number | Pattern} distortion amount of distortion to apply
{number | Pattern} volume linear postgain of the distortion
description: Distortion via Chebyshev polynomials

name: parray
description: Turns a list of patterns into a single pattern which outputs list-values

name: partials
params: {number[] | Pattern} magnitudes List of [0, 1] magnitudes for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental harmonic (i.e. DC offset is skipped)
description:
Scale the magnitude of the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', ..)

Can also be used to create a new synth via `s('user').partials(...)`

name: phases
params: {number[] | Pattern} phases List of [0, 1) phases for partials. 0th entry is the fundamental phase (i.e. DC offset is skipped)
description: Rotates the harmonics of one of the core synths ('sine', 'tri', 'saw', 'user', ..) by a list of phases

name: FX
description:
Establishes an FX chain. Can be called by chaining .FX(fx1).FX(fx2)..
calls and/or in a single .FX(fx1, fx2, ..) call. The fx1, .. are _patterns_ which
establish the controls of the given effect. See examples.
examples:
$: s("[sbd <hh [bd | lt | oh]>]*4").dec(.4)
.FX(
phaser(0.5).gain(2),
bpf(800),
distort(1.3),
room(0.2),
delay(0.5).gain(1.25),
distort(0.3),
).fxr(1.7) // sets release time of effects (like delay)

$: s("saw").fm(0.5)
.delay(0.3) // outer effects are applied *last*
.FX(coarse(4)) // first coarse
.FX(lpf(500).lpe(4).lpa(1).lpd(2)) // then lpf
.FX(distort(1)) // then distort

name: K
params: {KabelsalatExpression | Function} expr Kabelsalat graph definition
description:
Produces a [Kabelsalat](https://kabel.salat.dev/) modular sound engine.
This can be used as either an effect (by including `audioin()` at the beginning
of your kabel expression) or as a sound source (via any expression which doesn't
start with `audioin()`).

Some helpers you have available to you:
* Strudel mini notation works fine in K(..) via "" or ``
* More complex Strudel expressions (like "0 1 2".fast(4) or irand(24)) can be
written by wrapping them in `S(..)` inside your Kabel code
* We expose Strudel's note frequency under `sFreq` and Strudel's gate
information under `sGate`
* You can use more complex multi-line expressions (like `let x = a; let y = b; x.lpf(y);`)
by wrapping them inside a function in K (see example).
examples:
note("A c e".fast(4)).transpose("<0 2 4 6 8>")
.scale("F:minor").transpose("12")
.s("saw")
.K(
// audioin().mul(sGate.adsr(0.001, 0.3, 0, 0.2)) // as effect
saw(saw(sFreq / "2!3 16").mul(8).add(sFreq).lag("0!3 0.1")).mul(0.3) // as source
.mul(sGate.adsr(0, 0.15, 0.5, "0.1!3 1"))
.lpf(sGate.adsr(0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2).mul(1).add(0))
.add(x => x.delay(S("0.3 0.2".fast(2))).mul(0.7))
.add(x => x.delay("0.03 [0.08 0.01] 0.01 0.013").mul(0.77)).mul(0.7)
.add(x => x.delay(.13).mul(0.7))
.out()
)

name: worklet
params: {string} src Source code of the worklet update function
{...number | ...Pattern} inputs Worklet inputs
description:
Creates a worklet effect. Typically derived by writing K(...) in the REPL which will parse
Kabelsalat code.

name: base
params: {number} n - number to convert (can be a pattern or array)
{number} b - base to convert to (defaults to 10) (can be a pattern)
{number} d - max number of digits to produce for each n (defaults to 0 for all) (can be a pattern)
description:
Creates a pattern of numbers in base b from a number or pattern of numbers
limited to d digits long from the right

name: inhabit
params: {Pattern} pat
{*} xs
description:
Picks patterns (or plain values) either from a list (by index) or a lookup table (by name).
Similar to `pick`, but cycles are squeezed into the target ('inhabited') pattern.

name: inhabitmod
params: {Pattern} pat
{*} xs
description:
The same as `inhabit`, but if you pick a number greater than the size of the list,
it wraps around, rather than sticking at the maximum value.
For example, if you pick the fifth pattern of a list of three, you'll get the
second one.

name: setcpm
params: {number} cpm cycles per minute
description: Changes the global tempo to the given cycles per minute

name: mousex
description: The mouse's x position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: mousey
description: The mouse's y position value ranges from 0 to 1.

name: useRNG
params: {string} mod - Mode. One of 'legacy', 'precise'
description:
Sets which random number generator to use. Historically Strudel would
use `useRNG('legacy')`, which remains the default. To use a new more statistically
precise RNG, try `useRNG('precise')`.

name: binary
params: {number} n - input number to convert to binary
description: Creates a binary pattern from a number.

name: binaryN
params: {number} n - input number to convert to binary
{number} nBits - pattern length, defaults to 16
description: Creates a binary pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: binaryL
params:
{number} n - input number to convert to binary
s("saw").seg(8)
.partials(binaryL(irand(4096).add(1)))
description: Creates a binary list pattern from a number.

name: binaryNL
params: {number} n - input number to convert to binary
{number} nBits - pattern length, defaults to 16
description: Creates a binary list pattern from a number, padded to n bits long.

name: randL
params: {number} n Number of random numbers to sample
description: Creates a list of random numbers of the given length

name: shuffle
description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts in random order.
Each part will be played exactly once per cycle.

name: scramble
description:
Slices a pattern into the given number of parts, then plays those parts at random. Similar to `shuffle`,
but parts might be played more than once, or not at all, per cycle.

name: seed
params: {number} n A new seed. Can be any number.
description:
Change the seed for random signals. Normally, random signals depend on time,
so two patterns at the same time will have the same random values. Specifying
a new seed changes the signal output by `rand`. This also affects other functions
that use randomness, like `shuffle` and `sometimes`.
examples:
$: s("hh*4").degrade();
$: s("bd*4").degrade().seed(1); // Will degrade different events from the hi-hat

name: rand
description: A continuous pattern of random numbers, between 0 and 1.

name: brandBy
params: {number} probability - a number between 0 and 1
description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random), with a probability for the value being 1

name: brand
description: A continuous pattern of 0 or 1 (binary random)

name: irand
params: {number} n max value (exclusive)
description: A continuous pattern of random integers, between 0 and n-1.
examples:
// randomly select scale notes from 0 - 7 (= C to C)
n(irand(8)).struct("x x*2 x x*3").scale("C:minor")

name: perlin
description: Generates a continuous pattern of [perlin noise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perlin_noise), in the range 0..1.

name: berlin
description:
Generates a continuous pattern of [berlin noise](conceived by Jame Coyne and Jade Rowland as a joke but turned out to be surprisingly cool and useful,
like perlin noise but with sawtooth waves), in the range 0..1.

name: degradeBy
params: {number} amount - a number between 0 and 1
description:
Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 0% chance of removal
1 = 100% chance of removal

name: degrade
description: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.degradeBy(0.5)`

name: undegradeBy
params: {number} amount - a number between 0 and 1
description:
Inverse of `degradeBy`: Randomly removes events from the pattern by a given amount.
0 = 100% chance of removal
1 = 0% chance of removal
Events that would be removed by degradeBy are let through by undegradeBy and vice versa (see second example).

name: undegrade
description:
Inverse of `degrade`: Randomly removes 50% of events from the pattern. Shorthand for `.undegradeBy(0.5)`
Events that would be removed by degrade are let through by undegrade and vice versa (see second example).

name: sometimesBy
params: {number | Pattern} probability - a number between 0 and 1
{function} function - the transformation to apply
description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability.
Similar to `someCyclesBy`

name: sometimes
params: {function} function - the transformation to apply
description: Applies the given function with a 50% chance

name: someCyclesBy
params: {number | Pattern} probability - a number between 0 and 1
{function} function - the transformation to apply
description:
Randomly applies the given function by the given probability on a cycle by cycle basis.
Similar to `sometimesBy`

name: someCycles
description: Shorthand for `.someCyclesBy(0.5, fn)`

name: often
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.75, fn)`

name: rarely
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.25, fn)`

name: almostNever
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.1, fn)`

name: almostAlways
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0.9, fn)`

name: never
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(0, fn)` (never calls fn)

name: always
description: Shorthand for `.sometimesBy(1, fn)` (always calls fn)

name: whenKey
description:
Do something on a keypress, or array of keypresses
[Key name reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/UI_Events/Keyboard_event_key_values)

name: keyDown
description:
returns true when a key or array of keys is held
[Key name reference](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/UI_Events/Keyboard_event_key_values)

name: initDough
description: initializes dough ahead of time. you don't need to use this, but if you do, you can await it, so dough is ready before the pattern starts.

name: dough
description: Uses dough as the audio engine. more info at https://dough.strudel.cc

name: pianoroll
params: {Object} options Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:
{integer} cycles number of cycles to be displayed at the same time - defaults to 4
{number} playhead location of the active notes on the time axis - 0 to 1, defaults to 0.5
{boolean} vertical displays the roll vertically - 0 by default
{boolean} labels displays labels on individual notes (see the label function) - 0 by default
{boolean} flipTime reverse the direction of the roll - 0 by default
{boolean} flipValues reverse the relative location of notes on the value axis - 0 by default
{number} overscan lookup X cycles outside of the cycles window to display notes in advance - 1 by default
{boolean} hideNegative hide notes with negative time (before starting playing the pattern) - 0 by default
{boolean} smear notes leave a solid trace - 0 by default
{boolean} fold notes takes the full value axis width - 0 by default
{string} active hexadecimal or CSS color of the active notes - defaults to #FFCA28
{string} inactive hexadecimal or CSS color of the inactive notes - defaults to #7491D2
{string} background hexadecimal or CSS color of the background - defaults to transparent
{string} playheadColor hexadecimal or CSS color of the line representing the play head - defaults to white
{boolean} fill notes are filled with color (otherwise only the label is displayed) - 0 by default
{boolean} fillActive active notes are filled with color - 0 by default
{boolean} stroke notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default
{boolean} strokeActive active notes are shown with colored borders - 0 by default
{boolean} hideInactive only active notes are shown - 0 by default
{boolean} colorizeInactive use note color for inactive notes - 1 by default
{string} fontFamily define the font used by notes labels - defaults to 'monospace'
{integer} minMidi minimum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 10
{integer} maxMidi maximum note value to display on the value axis - defaults to 90
{boolean} autorange automatically calculate the minMidi and maxMidi parameters - 0 by default
description:
Visualises a pattern as a scrolling 'pianoroll', displayed in the background of the editor. To show a pianoroll for all running patterns, use `all(pianoroll)`. To have a pianoroll appear below
a pattern instead, prefix with `_`, e.g.: `sound("bd sd")._pianoroll()`.

name: wordfall
description:
Displays a vertical pianoroll with event labels.
Supports all the same options as pianoroll.

name: pitchwheel
params: {number} hapcircles
{number} circle
{number} edo
{string} root
{number} thickness
{number} hapRadius
{string} mode
{number} margin
description: Renders a pitch circle to visualize frequencies within one octave

name: spiral
params: {Object} options Object containing all the optional following parameters as key value pairs:
{number} stretch controls the rotations per cycle ratio, where 1 = 1 cycle / 360 degrees
{number} size the diameter of the spiral
{number} thickness line thickness
{string} cap style of line ends: butt (default), round, square
{string} inset number of rotations before spiral starts (default 3)
{string} playheadColor color of playhead, defaults to white
{number} playheadLength length of playhead in rotations, defaults to 0.02
{number} playheadThickness thickness of playheadrotations, defaults to thickness
{number} padding space around spiral
{number} steady steadyness of spiral vs playhead. 1 = spiral doesn't move, playhead does.
{number} activeColor color of active segment. defaults to foreground of theme
{number} inactiveColor color of inactive segments. defaults to gutterForeground of theme
{boolean} colorizeInactive wether or not to colorize inactive segments, defaults to 0
{boolean} fade wether or not past and future should fade out. defaults to 1
{boolean} logSpiral wether or not the spiral should be logarithmic. defaults to 0
description: Displays a spiral visual.

name: edoScale
params: {string} scale Definition of EDO scale.
description:
Turns numbers into notes in the given EDO scale (zero indexed).

An EDO scale definition looks like this:

e.g. C:LLsLLLs:2:1 <- this is the C major scale, 12 EDO

e.g. C:LLsLLL:3:1 <- this is the Gorgo 6 note scale, 16 EDO

An EDO scale, e.g. C:LLsLLLs:2:1, consists of a root note (e.g. C)
followed by semicolon (':')
and then a [Large/small step notation sequence](https://en.xen.wiki/w/MOS_scale)
(e.g. LLsLLLs)
followed by semicolon, then the large step size (e.g. 2)
followed by semicolon, then the small step size (e.g. 1).

The number of divisions of the octave is calculated as the sum
of the steps in the EDO scale definition.

e.g. C:LLsLLLs:2:1 is 2+2+1+2+2+2+1 = 12 EDO, 7 note scale

e.g. C:LLsLLL:3:1 is 3+3+1+3+3+3 = 16 EDO, 6 note scale

The root note defaults to octave 3, if no octave number is given.

name: midin
params: {string | number} input MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0
description:
MIDI input: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI control change messages.

The output is a function that accepts a midi cc value to query as well as (optionally) a midi channel
examples:
const cc = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')
note("c a f e").lpf(cc(0).range(0, 1000)).lpq(cc(1).range(0, 10)).sound("sawtooth")

const allCC = await midin('IAC Driver Bus 1')
const cc = (ccNum) => allCC(ccNum, 2) // just channel 2
note("c a f e").s("saw")
.when(cc(0).gt(0), x => x.postgain(0))

name: midikeys
params: {string | number} input MIDI device name or index defaulting to 0
description:
MIDI keyboard: Opens a MIDI input port to receive MIDI keyboard messages.

The note length is fixed as Superdough is not currently set up for undetermined
note durations

The 'midichan' control value contains the number of the channel the note is coming from
so it could be filtered or manipulated further in the chain.
examples:
const kb = await midikeys('Arturia KeyStep 32')
kb("0.5 1")
.s("saw")
.add(note(rand.mul(0.3)))
.lpf(1000).lpe(2).room(0.5)

name: accelerationY

name: accelerationZ

description: The device's rotation around the alpha-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.

description: The device's rotation around the beta-axis value ranges from 0 to 1.
